data.title: Rocket Lab Stock (RKLB) Rises Today, Sept. 15 — Here's What's Driving It
data.description:
Rocket Lab USA (RKLB) stock is up 3% at Tuesday's market open after the company completed its At-The-Market (ATM) share sale to finance its pending acquisition of Iridium Communications (IRDM). The company raised about $1.944 billion in gross proceeds through the issuance of 29.3 million shares.

For context, Rocket Lab agreed in June to acquire Iridium in a cash-and-stock deal that valued the satellite operator at about $8 billion, or $54 per share.

Rocket Lab Clears Key Financing Steps

On Sept. 15, Iridium amended its $1.775 billion term loan agreement to allow Rocket Lab's planned acquisition to move forward. After the deal closes, Rocket Lab USA will provide an unsecured guarantee for Iridium's term loan. The company also terminated its $3.6 billion commitment for a senior secured bridge facility that it entered into on June 28, 2026, as part of the merger agreement.

Rocket Lab plans to use the net proceeds from its ATM share sale to fund the cash portion of its Iridium acquisition. If the deal does not close or the company has money left over, it will use the funds for future growth and general business needs.

The Iridium deal is expected to close in mid-2027.

Rocket Lab Eyes Bigger Space Ambitions after Iridium Deal

Speaking to World Space Business Week, Rocket Lab CFO Adam Spice said Iridium could help transform the company from a launch provider into a more complete space business. He said the deal would expand the company beyond rocket launches and spacecraft manufacturing into satellite network operations and services.

Spice further said, "When you double your company overnight, which will be the case when we combine the companies, you'll naturally have some dilution in that growth."  Rocket Lab has grown by nearly 100% a year in recent years, while the more mature Iridium has grown at a single-digit rate. This means the acquisition could slow Rocket Lab's overall growth rate in the near term.

Still, Rocket Lab sees new growth opportunities in Iridium's business. Spice said better access to capital and a stronger focus on growth could help the combined company expand faster. "We've got a lot of aggressive plans" to bring growth closer to what investors expect, he added.

Is RKLB a Good Stock to Buy?

According to TipRanks, RKLB stock has received a Strong Buy consensus rating, with 14 Buys and three Holds assigned in the last three months. The average price target for Rocket Lab is $110.13, suggesting a potential upside of 76% from the current level.

data.title: Oracle Stock Forecast – Layoffs Mount as Analysts Remain Bullish
data.description:
Oracle (ORCL) stock remains under pressure as the company has reportedly begun another round of layoffs while continuing to invest billions of dollars in AI infrastructure. However, Wall Street analysts remain broadly bullish, betting that Oracle's rapidly growing AI cloud business can eventually justify its heavy spending.

The layoffs highlight Oracle's shift from a relatively people-intensive software business toward a more capital-intensive cloud and AI infrastructure model. In its latest annual report, Oracle cited AI adoption, strategic shifts, management and product changes, acquisitions, and efforts to improve operating efficiency among the factors behind workforce reductions.

Why Is Oracle Cutting Jobs?

In fiscal 2026, Oracle cut about 21,000 jobs, or 13% of its workforce, while spending $55.7 billion on capital expenditures, primarily to expand data centers. As of August 31, 2026, Oracle estimated that its 2026 restructuring plan could cost up to $2.1 billion. The company has also guided to roughly $70 billion in capital expenditures for the current fiscal year.

200% short exposure to ORCL with ORCZ

The workforce reductions come as Oracle aggressively expands its data-center footprint to meet demand for AI computing. The strategy is expensive, raising concerns about leverage, cash flow, and whether the company can generate sufficient returns from its AI investments.

Analysts Remain Bullish on ORCL

Despite the layoffs, analysts see reasons for optimism. Following Oracle's latest results, Freedom Broker analyst Egor Tolmachev lowered his price target on ORCL to $205 from $210 but maintained a Buy rating.

Tolmachev said Oracle's latest quarter provided stronger evidence that its AI investments are starting to drive revenue, pointing to a better-than-expected backlog, infrastructure revenue that more than doubled from the prior year, and an improved funding position.

However, he also raised some concerns. New bookings and backlog growth fell sharply from the previous quarter, while the company raised its guidance by less than expected. He also noted that profit grew slower than revenue, partly due to a lower tax rate and higher non-operating income.

He argued that investors need more evidence that Oracle can turn its massive contracted backlog into sustainable revenue and cash flow. He expects the company's October Investor Day to provide a more meaningful test of its AI plans.

What Is the Oracle Stock Forecast?

According to TipRanks, Oracle has a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 26 Buys and four Hold ratings. The average Oracle price target of $251.52 implies 73.7% upside potential from current levels. Year-to-date, ORCL shares have dropped 25%.

data.title: Musk Leaves Door Open to Tesla-SpaceX Merger as TSLA, SPCX Stocks Fall
data.description:
Elon Musk has given investors his clearest signal yet that he is open to combining Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX), though he stopped short of confirming that merger talks are underway.

Speaking at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles on Monday, Musk was asked why Tesla and SpaceX remain separate despite growing cooperation between the two companies. He called it a "great question" and pointed to their expanding ties across several areas.

"With all this collaboration, on so many levels, who can imagine what action one might take when there's so much close collaboration in so many areas," Musk said. He did not give a timeline, deal structure, or commitment.

SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell added to the speculation, saying the businesses were integrating "faster than I thought," while noting that they were "not fully integrated yet." She highlighted cooperation involving AI, computing, chips, solar-panel production, and personnel moving between Musk-controlled companies.

Both SPCX and TSLA stocks dropped yesterday 2.02% and 1.77%, respectively.

data.title: 'More Bang For the Buck,' Says Investor About Alphabet Stock
data.description:
The hyperscalers are putting their money where their mouth is, with hundreds of billions of dollars in capex set for this year and next. Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) is among the big spenders and is now guiding for $195 to $205 billion in spending in 2026 alone.

That's quite a pretty penny, and it has set off alarm bells among some investors. While the company has some exceptionally deep pockets, the spending has certainly depressed free cash flow. Alphabet even had a negative $5.9 billion in free cash flow last quarter, a pretty astounding statistic given its operating income of $40.8 billion in Q2.

In a sense, the giant outlay seems to be the price of doing business. After all, the demand is clearly there, as demonstrated by Google Cloud's backlog of $514 billion at the end of the quarter (growth of 82% year-over-year).

data.title: Crusoe-Perplexity AI Deal Highlights Demand for Nvidia GB300 Chips
data.description:
Data center operator Crusoe has signed a multiyear cloud agreement with Perplexity AI, giving the AI search company access to Nvidia Corporation (NVDA) chips for training and running its models. Financial terms were not disclosed, but the deal gives Crusoe another large AI customer as it expands beyond building data centers into renting computing capacity and software.

Perplexity will also rely on Crusoe to manage the hardware over its operating life. The companies are expanding the relationship in the other direction as well, with Crusoe providing Perplexity's Enterprise Max product to more than 1,800 employees.

The deal impacts Nvidia because Perplexity specifically wants access to its newer GB300 chips. Perplexity already uses cloud capacity from Amazon's (AMZN) Web Services and other large providers, but said Crusoe is helping it secure more of the Nvidia hardware it needs.

Promotion

Crusoe also offers chips from Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD), giving customers another option in a market where many AI cloud providers are heavily focused on Nvidia GPUs.

Crusoe Pushes Further Into CoreWeave's Market

Crusoe is best known for large data center projects, including OpenAI's Stargate site in Abilene, Texas. More recently, it has been building a cloud business that competes with providers including CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) by renting AI chips and related software directly to customers.

That effort has already produced a much larger contract. Earlier in September, Crusoe signed a roughly $13 billion cloud deal with Jane Street.

The Perplexity agreement is less detailed, since the companies did not disclose its value, but it broadens Crusoe's customer base and shows why access to scarce, high-end Nvidia hardware remains valuable to AI developers.

Crusoe's expansion also adds another competitor to a crowded AI infrastructure market that includes Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Corporation (MSFT)'s Azure and Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL)'s Google Cloud, along with newer providers such as CoreWeave.

The growth push comes as some of Crusoe's large data center projects have faced changes. OpenAI and Oracle Corporation (ORCL) declined to lease an expansion of the Abilene site, although Microsoft later agreed to rent the capacity, while Crusoe was also removed by partners from a Wyoming data center project being built for Google.

For public-market investors, the most important part of the Perplexity deal is the continued demand for advanced AI compute. Nvidia remains the clearest beneficiary of that demand, while AMD is trying to win more of the same workloads. For CoreWeave and the major cloud platforms, Crusoe's expansion adds another supplier competing for customers that want access to high-end AI chips without building their own data centers. The missing number is the value of the Perplexity contract, which will determine how meaningful the deal is financially for Crusoe compared with its much larger Jane Street agreement.

data.title: Nvidia and Micron: AI Slowdown Will Punish One AI Stock More Than the Other, Says Investor
data.description:
Calls to slow the pace of frontier AI development put the semiconductor sector back on edge on Monday. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei recently argued that the industry should "pace the frontier" to give companies more time for safety testing, oversight and governance, with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and other AI leaders generally supportive of the idea. The market reaction was immediate, with several semiconductor stocks selling off sharply as investors questioned whether slower model development could eventually mean less spending on AI infrastructure.

But slowing the development of ever-more-powerful models does not necessarily mean slowing AI infrastructure demand. The bigger shift may be from training the next frontier model toward running AI at enormous scale. As inference costs fall, companies can afford to use AI for more tasks, while agentic systems can generate huge numbers of tokens through repeated reasoning, planning and execution. That changes what matters in the semiconductor supply chain.

An investor with the moniker Summit Research (SR) argues that this distinction is particularly important when comparing Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Micron (NASDAQ:MU). Both benefit from AI spending, but their exposure is different, leaving Nvidia more vulnerable if the industry places less emphasis on rapid frontier upgrades.

Promotion

Discover why XOVR identified Kalshi as an attractive private investment opportunity.

For Nvidia, the problem is not that demand for compute disappears. Inference should remain a huge source of demand. The issue is that a slower frontier could reduce the urgency to buy Nvidia's newest and most powerful accelerators. If AI labs take an extra year or two between major model advances, customers may have less reason to rush into each new generation of hardware.

That matters because Nvidia has built its business around a rapid upgrade cycle. Each generation promises substantial gains in performance and efficiency, allowing the company to sell customers more powerful systems and support premium pricing. If frontier progress slows, however, the monetization of that annual cadence could become less predictable. Customers may continue buying Nvidia hardware, but they could put greater emphasis on cost-effective inference rather than paying up for maximum performance.

There is also a potential margin issue. Nvidia has argued that technological leadership and major performance-per-dollar improvements are central to sustaining its gross margins. A shift toward cheaper, inference-focused systems could therefore create a less favourable product mix, particularly if customers become less willing to pay for the very latest hardware.

Micron has a different exposure. Its HBM is tied closely to Nvidia and other AI accelerators, so a slowdown in frontier upgrades would still create some risk. But Micron also supplies server DRAM and NAND storage, areas that can benefit directly from the sheer volume of AI workloads.

Agentic AI requires large amounts of memory and storage to handle expanding context windows, KV caches and persistent data. That means Micron can benefit even when the AI industry is running more workloads on existing or less cutting-edge accelerators. Its opportunity is therefore tied more closely to the number of tokens being processed than to how quickly the frontier model itself advances.

SR also points to a crucial supply constraint. Micron has indicated that its HBM capacity is already accounted for well into 2028, while conventional DRAM is also facing tight supply. If frontier demand softens, capacity could potentially be redirected toward other memory products needed for large-scale inference.

That gives Micron a wider cushion. Nvidia remains heavily exposed to the pace of its accelerator upgrade cycle, while Micron can participate across several layers of the AI memory hierarchy.

As such, SR has downgraded Nvidia's rating to Hold (i.e., Neutral), while the investor maintained a Buy rating for Micron. (To watch Summit Research's track record, click here)

On the other hand, the Street has a bullish stance for both names, giving the pair Strong Buy consensus ratings. At $324.30, NVDA's average price target points toward 12-month returns of 54%. Micron's average target stands at $1,563.93, a figure offering one-year upside of 69%. (See Nvidia stock forecast or Micron stock forecast)

data.title: Stock Market Today, September 15 – Futures Slip as Treasury Yields Cross 5%, Rate Hike Looms
data.description:
U.S. stock futures fell ahead of Tuesday's session as surging oil prices fueled renewed inflation concerns, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield to 5.03%. Investors are awaiting the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on Wednesday. Markets are pricing in a 92% probability of a 0.25 percentage-point rate hike, which would raise the Fed's benchmark interest rate to 3.75%-4.00%.

Futures on the Nasdaq 100 (NDX), the S&P 500 Index (SPX), and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) were down 0.63%, 0.55%, and 0.67%, respectively, as of 5:38 a.m. EDT on September 15.

Oil prices extended gains on Tuesday as fresh attacks in the Gulf raised concerns about supply disruptions. Saudi Arabia also shut its key East-West oil pipeline, which bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, after drone attacks damaged it, further tightening supply. At the time of writing, Brent crude (CM:BZ) rose to $108.88 a barrel, while WTI crude (CM:CL) was near $104.03 a barrel.
